name: Sunshine and clouds (NASA)
summary: NASA's daily sunshine energy and cloud amount for each city, worked out from satellite cloud data. One value covers about 100 km and the newest day is about a week old.
tagline: NASA POWER · about a week behind

el.name: Ήλιος και σύννεφα (NASA)
el.summary: Η ημερήσια ηλιακή ενέργεια και η νέφωση κάθε πόλης από τη NASA, υπολογισμένες από δορυφορικά δεδομένα νεφών. Μία τιμή καλύπτει περίπου 100 χλμ. και η νεότερη μέρα είναι περίπου μιας εβδομάδας.
el.tagline: NASA POWER · περίπου μία εβδομάδα πίσω

licence.attribution: The data was obtained from the NASA Langley Research Center POWER Project (power.larc.nasa.gov)

restrictions: NASA asks for at most 5 requests at once and may block repeated requests for the same place
NASA asks users to cite POWER with the version number and the date the data was obtained

coverage.area: Global; solar values on a 1 degree grid

update.note: NASA updates nightly; solar values are about 5 to 7 days behind today.

variables.note: ALLSKY_SFC_SW_DWN, newest day NASA has (kWh per m2)

quality.uncertainty: Computed, not measured: satellite cloud observations feed a radiation model that also uses NASA weather-model inputs. A 100 km square cannot show a local cloud.
known_issues: A 1 degree grid cell is about 100 km wide, so nearby cities can get the same number
The newest day is about a week old, and the first estimates are later replaced by better ones
Cloud amount is a daily average over a big area, not the sky over the school at one moment
It is sunlight, not electricity: panel output also depends on size, angle, dirt, heat and efficiency; it is not lux either

use_for: A look at last week's sunshine and cloudiness for the region
Context for a talk about school solar panels
not_for: Anything about today or yesterday: the values are about a week old
Telling two nearby cities apart: they can share one 100 km cell
Saying how much electricity a solar panel makes

notes: Written from NASA's own pages on 2026-11-12 (the licence line is from the POWER listing on the AWS open-data registry). The service could not be called from the build sandbox. Unverified: the exact JSON, the unit POWER reports for community RE (the reader reads it and drops units it does not know), and that CLOUD_AMT is served for RE. After the deploy look in the Railway log for the line 'first answer'.
